The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-12T10:16:00Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-12T10:16:02Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-12T10:10:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-12T10:17:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 7 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 2 minutes 6 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-12T10:18:09Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.9% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 28.9% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 40.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 27.9% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9416666666666667% {series_before} before it began, 28.85714285714286% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 40.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 4,486.73 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-12T10:16:02Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-12T10:16:04Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-12T10:16:04Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-12T10:16:05Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 10:16 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-12T10:16:05Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 361 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-12T10:16:05Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 10:10 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-12T10:16:05Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-12T10:16:08Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 12 10:11 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-12T10:16:08Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-12T10:16:08Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-12T10:16:08Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 {T11.2} minutes before 10:16 {T11.3}
  - [T12] 2026-11-12T10:16:08Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 124 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-12T10:16:12Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-12T10:16:12Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-12T10:16:12Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 10:16:12 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-12T10:16:13Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-12T10:16:13Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-12T10:16:13Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
  - [T19] 2026-11-12T10:16:14Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 10:17 {T19.2} - up to 166s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-12T10:18:09Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 10:16 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-12T10:18:09Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-12T10:18:09Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [monthly-spend-feature] OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T23] 2026-11-12T10:19:03Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/570

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-12T10:10:31Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 30 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 30 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 09:40–10:09 {G7e5d.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 30 {G46bc.2} minutes, 09:40–10:09 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 37 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 09:40–10:16 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 40.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 10:13 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 26 {Gad41.2} minutes, 09:41–10:06 {Gad41.3}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 {G971b.1} / on 99 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 10:10 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 10:10–10:16 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 10:11–10:16 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 2026-11-12T10:10:31Z {C1.1}. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to 20-40% {C1.3}. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py returns `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)`, where `bought_this_month` is the purchases flagged `in_current_month`. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has an empty list there, so the line raises ZeroDivisionError. That is not an edge case. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls it "the ordinary case". With monthly-spend-feature off, `render_spend_summary` never reached this function. With it on, every such shopper's request reached it, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turned each error into a failed page.
      
      The change: if there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0 {F1.1}. Nothing was spent per item this month, and `total_this_month_cents` is itself 0 {F1.2} for such an account in the fixtures. Otherwise the division is unchanged. With the flag off, nothing changes. `average_spend_per_item` and the lifetime path are untouched. They still raise for an account that has never bought anything, which the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py and tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py rely on. `render_spend_summary` and `serve_account_page` still get an int, so their return types and callers are unchanged.
      
      The tests: three new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py. Two call the monthly figure directly and through `render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True)` for a shopper with no purchases this month, and expect 0 {F1.3}. One expects 0 {F1.4} for a shopper with no history at all when the monthly flag is on. Each of these would raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code. The test that expects a failure to reach the caller on the lifetime path stays as it is.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #570 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month` and does not handle an empty list. So for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns that error into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary made the account page fail with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought before but not yet this month.
still_at_risk: Switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again in the same way.
symptom: Account pages failed for shoppers
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 during {G5309.3}. No such error was logged before then. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at {P1.1}. Before that it was evaluated off and account pages rendered normally. Evaluations were split between off and on at {G971b.6} and were all on during {Gce95.4}. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read. (cites T15, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 4: With the flag on, account page requests reached a monthly per-item spend calculation that divides by zero for shoppers with no purchases this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: The flag change reached all account page traffic almost at once: evaluations were split briefly and then all on. No staged rollout or health check that would hold back or undo a flag change was seen.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout gated on the error rate would have kept the failures to a small share of shoppers and stopped the change before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors 2: No test of the flag-on path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month was seen before the flag was switched on. Code-Fix says the cases it adds would raise against the current code.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been caught before the flag was switched on in production.
action_items 1: Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop in stages, with an error-rate check that stops the rollout and turns the flag back off when errors rise.
action_items 2: Require tests that exercise a flag's on path to pass in CI before that flag can be switched on in production.
action_items 3: Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
